title: Sell Mineral Rights in Adamsburg, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Adamsburg, PA | Westmoreland
metaDescription: Adamsburg mineral owners in Westmoreland County: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus royalty, explained plainly, no obligation.
heroLead: Adamsburg is a small borough near where the Sewickley Creek watershed and Westmoreland County's active Marcellus leasehold overlap.
intro: Westmoreland County came a little later to the Marcellus boom than its neighbors to the west, but development has been steady here for over a decade now, and Adamsburg-area families with farm or legacy land have largely been part of it. If you hold minerals here, the interest likely traces back to a lease signed during that buildout, and the royalty checks since have moved around in ways that probably never got fully explained.
We've been the family staring at a confusing statement too, wondering what a number actually meant. That's why we walk through your paperwork with you before anything else.

sections.heading: Westmoreland's later, still-real Marcellus wave
paragraphs: Operators including EQT and CNX have leased and drilled substantially across Westmoreland County, with development spreading eastward from the more heavily drilled Washington and Greene County core over the years. Adamsburg sits in territory that saw real leasing activity, and many local tracts are pooled into units even where the well pad itself sits some distance away.

This part of the county is generally wet-gas Marcellus, meaning natural gas liquids make up a real share of production, with the processing costs to separate them typically deducted from your royalty before it's paid.

sections.heading: Understanding your specific unit
paragraphs: Because pooled units can span multiple properties and even multiple owners with very different lease terms, two Adamsburg-area families can hold identical acreage and see very different royalty checks depending on when their lease was signed and what deduction language it contains. We review your actual lease, not a general assumption, before quoting a number.

sections.heading: What we check before an offer
paragraphs: We confirm your chain of title through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds, verify your decimal interest in the applicable unit, and review recent royalty statements so the offer reflects your real production history.

faqs.question: Is Westmoreland County as active as Washington County for gas drilling?
faqs.answer: It's developed somewhat later and less intensively overall, but there's real, sustained leasing and drilling activity across much of the county, including around Adamsburg.

faqs.question: Two neighbors with similar acreage have very different royalty checks. Why?
faqs.answer: Lease terms, deduction language, and unit participation percentage can vary significantly even between adjacent tracts, especially if the leases were signed years apart.

faqs.question: How do you confirm what unit my tract is part of?
faqs.answer: We cross-reference your parcel against Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection well and unit records to confirm participation before making an offer.
